Here's how he earned it. |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/knicks/2026/06/05/jalen-brunson-nickname-captain-clutch-knicks-spurs-nba-finals/90411628007/ |access-date=June 19, 2026 |work=USA TODAY |date=June 5, 2026}}</ref> and the "'''King of New York'''",{{efn|Per ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'',<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/sports/basketball/jalen-brunson-new-york-knicks-nba-finals-ac6b287d?|title=Jalen Brunson Is the 'King of New York'|last=Gay|first=Jason|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|date=June 14, 2026}}</ref> [[ESPN]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48995150/how-jalen-brunson-became-king-new-york-knicks-nba-finals|title=How Jalen Brunson became the undisputed king of New York|last=Shelburne|first=Ramona|date=June 13, 2026|work=ESPN}}</ref> and ''[[The New York Times]]''<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7358437/2026/06/14/jalen-brunson-greatest-knicks-nba-championship/|title=Jalen Brunson, NBA champion and finals MVP, is officially the greatest Knick ever|work=The New York Times|url-access=subscription|date=June 14, 2026|last=Edwards III|first=James L.}}</ref> among others.}} is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). The son of former NBA guard [[Rick Brunson]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]], earning [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national player of the year]] honors as a [[junior (education year)|junior]] and winning two national championships. Brunson was selected 33rd overall in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and played his first four NBA seasons with them. He signed with the Knicks as a free agent in 2022, subsequently leading the franchise to its [[2026 NBA Finals|first NBA championship in 53 years]].

Brunson participated in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. He led [[Stevenson High School (Lincolnshire, Illinois)|Stevenson]] to the [[Illinois High School Association]] (IHSA) Class 4A championship. He won [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] and [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|was named the MVP]] of the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]. Brunson was a role player for the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|championship season]] of the [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|2015–16 Villanova Wildcats]] and named the [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national player of the year]] and a consensus first-team [[2018 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2018 All-American]] for the [[2018 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|championship season]] of the [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|2017–18 Wildcats]]. After being selected by the Mavericks, Brunson spent four seasons with Dallas, culminating in a run to the [[NBA conference finals|Western Conference Finals]].

Since joining the Knicks in 2022, Brunson has been named an NBA All-Star three times ({{nasg|2024}}–{{nasg|2026}}) and received three [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA Second Team]] selections in the same period. He set the NBA record for most three-point shots made in a half without a miss (8), and tied the NBA record for most three-point shots made in a single game without a miss (9). In 2025, he led the Knicks to their first Eastern Conference Finals appearance in 25 years. In 2026, he led the franchise to its first [[NBA Finals]] appearance since 1999 and its first NBA championship since 1973, earning both the [[NBA conference finals MVP awards|Eastern Conference Finals MVP]] and the [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player|NBA Finals MVP]]. He also tied [[Michael Jordan]]’s record for most points scored in a title clinching road finals game (45) which Jordan set back in [[1998 NBA Finals|1998]] against the [[Utah Jazz]].

}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks' Jalen Brunson: Game-high 36 points in win|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/knicks-jalen-brunson-game-high-36-points-in-win/|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=June 11, 2026|access-date=June 11, 2026}}</ref> With 33 points by [[OG Anunoby]], it was the first time two Knicks scored at least 30 points in an NBA Finals game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-vs-spurs-game-notes-june-13-2026-nba-finals-game-5|title=Knicks vs Spurs Game Notes: June 13, 2026: NBA Finals - Game 5|accessdate=June 14, 2026|date=June 13, 2026|publisher=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref> In Game 5, Brunson put up 45 points to lead the Knicks to a 94–90 win and close out the NBA Finals against the Spurs, 4–1, securing the Knicks' first NBA championship in 53 years. Brunson became the eighth player to win NBA Finals MVP after winning an NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament.<ref name=KJBjMJKAaftarcf/> He became one of only five players in basketball history to win an NCAA national championship, the Naismith College Player of the Year Award, an NBA championship, and the NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award, joining [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]], [[Magic Johnson]], Michael Jordan, and [[Bill Walton]]. <ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks' Jalen Brunson joins Michael Jordan, Kareem among few to achieve remarkable feat |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/knicks-jalen-brunson-nba-finals-mvp-champion-ncaa-college/ |website=CBS Sports |date=2026-06-14 |access-date=2026-06-14}}</ref> Brunson became the fourth player to win the NBA Finals MVP after winning an NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament and a state high school championship, joining Abdul-Jabbar, Walton, and Johnson.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/new-york-knicks/news/jalen-brunson-bill-russell-championship-trifecta/b0d8dd3b8af45c209dacfb3e|title=Jalen Brunson joins Bill Russell, Magic Johnson in exclusive club with championship trifecta|accessdate=June 17, 2026|date=June 14, 2026|work=[[The Sporting News]]|author=Treacy, Dan}}</ref><ref name=KJBjMJKAaftarcf>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/knicks-jalen-brunson-nba-finals-mvp-champion-ncaa-college/|title=Knicks' Jalen Brunson joins Michael Jordan, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar among few to achieve remarkable career feat|accessdate=June 17, 2026|date=June 14, 2026|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|author=Silverstein, Adam}}</ref> He also become one of only four second round NBA draft picks to be named the NBA Finals MVP, joining [[Willis Reed]], [[Dennis Johnson]], and [[Nikola Jokić]].<ref name=NKsuthtfei5cd/>

==Playing style==
Brunson is known for having elite footwork, but not elite athleticism.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40049687/nba-playoffs-2024-jalen-brunson-ruthless-old-man-game-driving-new-york-knicks-playoff-run |title=NBA playoffs 2024: Jalen Brunson and the ruthless old-man game driving the New York Knicks |access-date=May 1, 2024 |date=April 30, 2024 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |author=Herring, Chris |archive-date=April 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430220300/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40049687/nba-playoffs-2024-jalen-brunson-ruthless-old-man-game-driving-new-york-knicks-playoff-run |url-status=live}}</ref> Brunson describes himself as a "hustle player".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/posts/jalen-brunson-new-york-knicks-nba-basketball |title=To My New York Family |access-date=May 3, 2024 |date=April 18, 2024 |author=Brunson, Jalen |work=[[The Players' Tribune]]}}</ref> Brunson draws a high number of offensive fouls.
